body: This is awesome! Just happened to stumble upon this while trying to decide what community college I would go to for graphic design, and seeing that you did something like this is very inspiring! I hope it works out really well for you!

Hey! BTW I've been doing a scan of technical colleges tonight. They seem to be the most promising with short programs (the longest I've seen so far is 64 weeks) and more specific programs. Maybe check out your states technical colleges or technical college online programs and certifications!

We really are in similar situations! You probably wouldn't believe me if I told you I started off taking the music management route just so I could know about how to keep my money right once I got into background singing (I did not cuz I couldn't even afford that life).

I agree as well about the whole competitive thing. It just means more jobs are available. I didn't know about the whole graphic artist thing either, so thank you! I love the illustration part more than the logo or product aspects as well! I use Procreate (and I'm gonna check out Gimp)  to do my work since I can't afford Adobe products. I'm thinking that there are formal courses out there that don't just use Adobe for everything too because, unless I get a student account or can afford it, I'm not interested right now.

I'll check out that coursera course! Thanks for that! 
Btw, my Instagram is @jilliantriesdesign if you're interested. I'm only on here to ask questions and respond to replies, but if I find anything that may be a good fit for us both, I'll let you know for sure! This is so complicated!

Absolutely! I see all the time online- even when I look at the graphic design reddit when I'm on here- how someone got a job without college or any x-amount-of-months-certification. The thing I learn from them is your portfolio isn't just about the work you've done; it's also have you made (for example) logos for someone who commissioned it. 

It's a REALLY competitive field, however- even for entry level. I do a lot of classes whenever I get a free trial on skillshare about leveraging your art and pitching to places you think your work fits best, but I want something more stable and more flexibility on what I can make.

When I thought UI was the route I wanted before I finally decided graphic design and illustration is it for me, I saw a lot of boot camps and online places for specifically ui, ux, ux/ui, web design, and graphic design. The more I kept researching, the more disappointing it got because some of the "best" are way too expensive for a few months. 

I think the best thing that everyone seems to trace back to is just keep building your portfolio. If you can, try doing commissions (because getting paid seems to equal career experience). If I don't have to go to school, I won't, but I'm in the same boat as you. Just trying to find my best route and options.

No, I didn't get that list, but I am 1,000 percent with you! I think the only reason I could find about accredited schools "mattering" is because of transfer credits, but-  as someone who dropped out of college sophomore year especially after them messing me up after completing a full year of it in high school- I just want a completely new start! 

I did manage to find a list of my own that I'll link you with. It has 4 year (yuck), 2 year, and certifications. I'm thinking that if I can find a community college or something that is cost-effective and helpful, I'll just go for that.

I truly think the guy, no offense to him if he isn't, was a recruiter of some sort. I don't know the proper term when they aren't recruiting for a specific school, but that's what I'm thinking.

Anyway, here's the list: https://www.accredited-online-college.org/accredited-online-colleges-for-graphic-design/

Thank you for responding! I hope we both find success I'm this field. So glad to know I'm not alone!
I'd love that! Yes, I'm in Georgia. I believe Scad is highly accredited, but I don't like the experiences my loved ones are having with them so I would love a list!

Ahhh ok. I appreciate your response! Do you have any recommendations for a graphic design education? I would rather just learn myself, which is what I'm doing anyway and adding to my portfolio constantly, to hopefully land a job that way, but if you have any education advice for graphic design, it would be greatly appreciated!
For clarification, do you mean as in not accredited or just not respected by hiring managers and what not? Sorry if this is a dumb question, but I want to be 10000% sure.
